title: Higher direct images of quasi-coherent modules on qcqs algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and suppose $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated: inverse images of quasi-compact spaces are quasi-compact and the diagonal of $f$ is quasi-compact. For every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $F$ on the small etale ringed site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and every $i\geq0$, the module $R^if_*F$ is quasi-coherent on $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$. Here $f_*$ is the canonical module direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], and $R^if_*$ is computed by injective resolutions in all module sheaves [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. No Noetherian, finite-type, coherence or separatedness assumption beyond the stated quasi-separatedness is imposed.

proof.text: It suffices to prove the assertion after every affine etale chart $V\to Y$. Indeed quasi-coherence is a local-presentation condition: the presentations on a covering of each affine chart compose to covering presentations on each object of $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$; arbitrary scheme charts have affine open covers. Restricting $F$ to $X_V=X\times_YV$ preserves its local presentations. The higher-image restriction isomorphism identifies the desired restriction with $R^if_{V,*}(F|_{X_V})$. Quasi-compactness is stable under base change by the cited affine-test lemma; the relative diagonal of $f_V$ is the base change of that of $f$, so the same stability proves quasi-separatedness. Hence replace $Y$ by $V$.

source.place: Tag 0720, first paragraph; affine-chart localization and the alternative relative Cech proof announced before the lemma.

proof.text: Now $Y$ is affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Quasi-compactness of $f$ gives quasi-compactness of $X$, and the source clause of the qcqs-product lemma gives quasi-separatedness of $X$. For this absolute formulation regard spaces over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ by the cited change-of-base identification. The cited atlas/topology equivalence identifies this quasi-compactness with quasi-compactness of the point space, as required by the atlas and permanence statements. Choose an affine surjective etale scheme chart $U\to X$. For $p\geq0$ put $U_p=U^{\times_X(p+1)}$. Inductively $U_p$ is a scheme: $U_0=U$, and $U_p\times_XU$ is the base change of the representable etale map $U\to X$ to the scheme $U_p$. It is qcqs by induction and the qcqs-product clause. The permanence lemma therefore says $a_p:U_p\to Y$ is qcqs, and the affine-test equivalence identifies this with scheme quasi-compactness; its diagonal has the same scheme tests for quasi-separatedness.

source.place: Tag 0720, affine atlas paragraph; relative Cech proof: all iterated atlas fibre products are qcqs schemes.

proof.text: Let $F_p=F|_{U_p}$. Each $u_p:U_p\to X$ is etale (successive base changes and compositions of the atlas), so restriction preserves the local free presentations defining quasi-coherence. Apply the relative Cech module spectral sequence to $f$ and this atlas. Its first page is $E_1^{p,q}=R^qa_{p,*}F_p$ and it converges to $R^{p+q}f_*F$ with the specified finite filtration. Every $a_p$ is a qcqs scheme morphism by step 2; the scheme small-etale higher-image comparison therefore makes every $E_1^{p,q}$ quasi-coherent. This uses structure-sheaf modules throughout.

source.place: Relative Cech alternative preceding Tag 0720; Tag 071N for the scheme terms; Tag 072E for the spectral sequence.

proof.text: Every later page is quasi-coherent, by induction on the page: at each bidegree the next page is the cokernel of the map from the incoming image to the outgoing kernel. These images and kernels, and then that cokernel, are quasi-coherent by the cited closure statement. At fixed $(p,q)$ first-quadrant differentials vanish for sufficiently large page (an incoming differential requires $r\leq p$, an outgoing one requires $r\leq q+1$). Thus the stable term $E_\infty^{p,q}$ is quasi-coherent. No closure under arbitrary subobjects is used.

source.place: Relative Cech alternative to Tag 0720: page induction using Tag 03M1, clauses (2),(3).

proof.text: For fixed $i\geq0$, convergence gives $F^0=R^if_*F$ and $F^{i+1}=0$ with $F^p/F^{p+1}=E_\infty^{p,i-p}$. The zero module is quasi-coherent (its zero presentation). Descending finite induction on $p=i,\ldots,0$ applies extension closure to $0\to F^{p+1}\to F^p\to E_\infty^{p,i-p}\to0$. It gives quasi-coherence of $F^0$. Step 1 then gives the assertion on the original $Y$, including $i=0$.

source.place: Relative Cech alternative to Tag 0720: finite abutment filtration and Tag 03M1(4).
